title: Applications by Fathers for Full Paternity Leave
what_it_is: Applications by Fathers for Full Paternity Leave

sections.label: Paternity leave applications and Civil Service
sections.summary: Figures on eligible working fathers applying for a full week of paid paternity leave in 2016 are still increasing and will be finalised at end of March 2018; 16% of applications are from the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) how many eligible working fathers have applied for a full week of paid paternity leave in 2016; and (b) what is the percentage of applications from the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: This figure is still increasing as fathers have the flexibility to take Paternity Leave up to 12 months after their child's birth.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The figures will only be finalised at the end of March 2018, when the deadline for the submission of claims is over.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Sixteen percent of these applications are from the Civil Service.

sections.label: Paternity leave take-up rates
sections.summary: 11,300 fathers had applied, with 16% of the whole number; take-up rates were about 38.5% in 2014, 44.1% in 2015 and 35.7% in 2016 as at to date.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In my answer earlier, I mentioned that 11,300 fathers had applied and 16% is with regard to the whole number and the base that we have.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In 2014, we had about 38.5% take-up rate; in 2015, it was 44.1%; in 2016, as at to date, it is 35.7%.

sections.label: Civil Service eligible fathers applications
sections.summary: As at to date, 91.4% of eligible fathers in the Civil Service have applied for this leave.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As at to date, 91.4% of eligible fathers in the Civil Service have applied for this leave.

sections.label: Reaching out to employers
sections.summary: They have been reaching out to employers to develop family-friendly workplaces and environment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As such, we have been reaching out to employers to develop family-friendly workplaces and environment.
